title: ALMA Survey of Orion Planck Galactic Cold Clumps (ALMASOP): A Hot Corino Survey toward Protostellar Cores in the Orion Cloud
question: What is the occurrence rate and possible origin of complex organic molecules (COMs) and hot corinos toward protostellar cores in the Orion cloud?

data.sensitivity: ~2.8 mJy beam^-1 per 1.129 MHz channel (~0.5 K); ~12 uJy beam^-1 for continuum

what.value: Bolometric temperature, bolometric luminosity, YSO classification, archival SED flux data points from 3.6 um to 870 um, and outflow effective opening angles at 400 au

evidence.quote: $T_\mathrm{bol}$ and $L_\mathrm{bol}$are bolometric temperature and bolometric luminosity adapted from (cite: 2020Dutta_ALMASOP).
The archival SED data of the 11 sources collected by (cite: 2020Dutta_ALMASOP) cover from 3.6 $\mu$m to 870 $\mu$m.

evidence.loc: Additional Constraint to the Cavity of YSO Model
evidence.quote: From (cite: 2020Dutta_ALMASOP), we adopt the effective opening angle at 400 au ($\Theta_\mathrm{400}$)

what.value: Distances to Orion A (398 pc), Orion B (404 pc), and lambda Orionis (404 pc) clouds

evidence.quote: the distance $D$ was fixed to be 398 pc, 404 pc, and 404 pc, respectively, for sources in the Orion A, Orion B, and $\lambda$ Orionis clouds (cite: 2018Kounkel_Orion_distance).

what.value: 12C/13C isotope ratio of 50 in the Orion cloud

evidence.loc: Luminosity and Warm Region in Hot Corino
evidence.quote: We use $^{13}$CH$_3$OH with $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C $=$ 50 (cite: 2018Kahane_13C12C_Orion) to derive the methanol column density

what.value: PEACHES survey warm methanol detection rates and COM column densities in Perseus

evidence.quote: We further compare the detection rate of warm methanol in ALMASOP with that found by PEACHES, which is a census of COMs conducted with ALMA toward embedded protostars in the Perseus cloud by (cite: 2021Yang_PEACHES).

what.value: Molecular spectroscopic parameters from CDMS and JPL databases

evidence.quote: The data are exported from XCLASS and adapted from CDMS (cite: 2005CDMS) and JPL (cite: 1988JPL).

recipe.goal: Preliminary search for COMs and source selection
recipe.method: Extract spectra at the 1.3 mm continuum peak pixel for all 56 Class 0/I protostellar cores and select sources with at least two CH3OH transitions detected at SNR > 5 (including at least one with E_up > 100 K).
key_parameters: At least one transition with E_up > 100 K

recipe.goal: Measure source emission size and H2 column density, and extract source-averaged spectra
recipe.method: Perform 2D Gaussian fitting on the CH3OH-46K (218440 MHz) moment-0 images in CASA to define the emission extent, extract full spectra within this extent, and compute H2 column density N(H2) from 1.3 mm continuum flux within the same extent.
key_parameters: Reference line: CH3OH J=4-3, Ka=2-1, Kc=3-2 at 218440 MHz (E_up = 46 K)
assumptions: Dust opacity law kappa_nu = 0.1 (nu / 1 THz)^beta cm^2 g^-1 with beta = 1.70

recipe.goal: Identify molecular transitions and fit LTE synthetic spectra
recipe.method: Use XCLASS LineIdentification to identify molecular carriers and simulate 1D LTE synthetic spectra to fit T_ex, N, delta_v, and v_LSR for each species, first individually and then simultaneously for all species to account for line blending.
key_parameters: T_ex range limited to (0, 400) K for initial fitting
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) for each gaseous molecular component
Emission size of all species equals the deconvolved 2D Gaussian extent of the CH3OH-46K transition
T_ex = 100 K fixed for molecules detected with only one transition

recipe.goal: Fit YSO spectral energy distributions (SEDs) and reconstruct thermal structure
recipe.method: Combine archival 3.6-870 um photometry with 1.3 mm ALMASOP ACA and combined peak flux densities, fit against the Robitaille et al. (2006) YSO model grid using SED Fitter with observational constraints on disk outer radius and outflow cavity opening angle, and reconstruct the 2D thermal structure using HO-CHUNK (2008 version) to measure the >100 K warm region size.
key_parameters: Fixed distances D = 398 pc (Orion A), 404 pc (Orion B), 404 pc (lambda Orionis)
Disk outer radius constraint < 140 au (except G192)
Outflow cavity effective opening angle constraint |Theta_400^Fitter - Theta_400^obs| < 1 deg
Magnetospheric truncation radius R_trunc = 5 R_* and hot spot fractional area f_spot = 0.007
assumptions: 2D axisymmetric YSO geometry (central star, accretion disk, envelope, bipolar cavity) with solar metallicity PHOENIX stellar atmospheres

recipe.goal: Evaluate statistical correlations, detection rates, and chemical abundance ratios
recipe.method: Calculate total gas-phase methanol molecule numbers from 13CH3OH (scaled by 12C/13C = 50), correlate with L_bol, compare hot corino detection rates with ACA-only data and the Perseus PEACHES survey under matched criteria, and fit linear proportional relations to COM column densities.
key_parameters: PEACHES-matched criteria: L_bol > 1 L_sun and 3 sigma methanol detection
assumptions: 12C/13C = 50 in the Orion cloud to rescale 13CH3OH column density to main CH3OH

evidence.quote: We report the detection of 11 hot corino sources, which exhibit compact emissions from warm and abundant COMs, among 56 Class 0/I protostellar cores.

answer_key.quantity: Hot corino detection rate in ALMASOP combined data

evidence.quote: The combined effect results in an increased detection rate of warm methanol from 8% in (cite: Hsu2020_ALMASOP) to 20% in this work.

score_reason: The paper clearly states the ALMA project code, CASA version, tclean robust parameter, cleaning thresholds, and provides complete tables of fitted molecular parameters (Tables 6-16), source sizes (Table 4), and SED best-fit models (Table 20), plus a detailed appendix on HO-CHUNK parameters. However, calibration/continuum-subtraction details, moment-0 velocity integration ranges, and exact XCLASS fitting scripts/priors are omitted or deferred to companion papers.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Cycle 6 dataset (2018.1.00302.S) with well-defined quantitative outputs (11 hot corino detections, CH3OH source sizes, N(H2), and XCLASS LTE parameters T_ex, N, delta_v, v_LSR for 36 species) that can be directly compared against an independent spectral extraction and LTE fitting pipeline.
